solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Glass fitter less inclined to work after end of morning

indicators.note: after places the lazy word behind the picked letter in the charade
end of picks out the final letter of morning

parts.note: lazier means less inclined to make an effort

explanation.surface: A tradesman who fits windows grows idle once the morning is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts LAZIER behind G, the last letter of 'morning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who cuts and installs window panes is called by this name.

clue.text: Become flustered, as visitor entering America will?

definitions.meaning: to get worked up, agitated or anxious
someone arriving in the USA literally goes into one of its fifty states

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: America is made up of states, so any visitor goes into one.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for working oneself into agitation or a panic.

clue.text: Pilot taking a bomb to a great height

parts.note: the V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, written here as VI
a tor is a high rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A wartime airman carries his bomb up to a lofty altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: V1 is written with the letter I for the digit 1. A TOR is a rocky hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flies aircraft; the older formal word for one is a synonym.

clue.text: Is Buddhist priest supervising wicked city?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supervising means sitting over, so the priest comes above the next piece

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest
wicked means bad

explanation.surface: A question whether a Buddhist cleric is in charge of a sinful city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supervising' places LAMA above BAD in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan.

clue.text: Prepare for publication Soviet law?

parts.note: red stands for communist, as in the Soviet Union
an act is a law passed by a parliament

explanation.surface: Is this a piece of Soviet legislation being readied for print?
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to edit a text into shape for printing, or to censor parts of it.

clue.text: Agreement in the bag, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means we hear it spoken, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: something in a bag has been packed

explanation.surface: Someone says a deal is as good as done: in the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' signals that PACKED is said aloud, giving a word of the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement or treaty between parties.

clue.text: Secure parking, for example

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Fix a parking space in place, say.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something down with a pin or stake, as with a tent.

clue.text: Leaders of lefties thrown into prison, innocent of charges

indicators.note: thrown into says the picked letters are put inside the jail word

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: leaders, in the plural, takes the opening two letters of lefties

explanation.surface: Left-wing ringleaders are jailed although they did nothing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Plural 'Leaders' takes two opening letters, not one; 'thrown into' places them inside 'can', American slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a spotless record has nothing against them; the word also means free from guilt.

clue.text: Fabric wife left in drawer

indicators.note: left in means placed inside, so the wife letter is deposited within the drawer word

parts.note: a till is a cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: Some cloth a wife has put away in a drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is a verb here (deposited), not the direction: W goes inside TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a textile woven with diagonal ribs, like denim.

clue.text: Soldier comes round wearing clothes for ramble

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the clothing word wraps the soldier

parts.note: dress means clothes

indicators.note: comes round means turns about, so the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier recovers consciousness while in uniform, ready for a long walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' reads as waking up, but turns the American serviceman backwards; 'wearing' wraps the outfit around him. 'ramble' means wander off topic, not hike.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander off the subject when speaking is to stray from the point, the verbal sense of ramble.

clue.text: Mother rates unusually small house

indicators.note: unusually says the letters are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A mother gives an odd verdict on a modest home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the letters of MOTHER RATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-time buyer's modest property, the first rung on the housing ladder.

clue.text: Fruit enthusiast

definitions.meaning: a hard-shelled seed such as a walnut or hazelnut
a fanatic, as in a fitness fan

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hard-shelled fruit and an obsessive fan.

clue.text: Country club teacher finds wonderful? The reverse

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: the reverse means the excellent word is turned backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I

explanation.surface: A golf club's coach finds something marvellous, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' turns AI (A1, first-class) into IA. A DON is a teacher at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: North Macedonia is a Balkan nation, long known by the shorter name.

clue.text: Reckless lawyer getting terribly reviled

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

indicators.note: terribly shows the letters of reviled are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A rash attorney finds himself badly vilified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges REVILED into REDEVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it describes someone bold to the point of recklessness.

clue.text: Gets rid of surgeons' clothing

definitions.meaning: cancels or removes, as in deleting a plan
the loose cotton outfits worn in operating theatres

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means cancels or washes away; the noun is the hospital garb surgeons wear.

clue.text: Wayward shoplifter ran through stores

indicators.note: stores means keeps inside, so the word is held within these clue words

explanation.surface: A wayward shoplifter dashes through the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stores' looks like shops but means contains: the answer runs inside 'shoplifter ran through'.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying from the proper course or behaving badly, like a knight errant who roams.

clue.text: Warning about British approaching a region of Canada

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the warning goes round the British letter

parts.note: an alert is a warning

explanation.surface: An alert issued about Britons heading towards western Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ALERT round B.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is one of the Canadian provinces, home to Calgary and Edmonton.

clue.text: Catch husband or wife briefly getting upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read from bottom to top
briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a spouse is a partner

explanation.surface: A spouse is caught out and gets briefly annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts PARTNER to PARTNE; 'getting upset' turns that upside down in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap or ensnare someone, especially by trickery.

clue.text: A group on ecstasy and speed, ultimately very wild

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, picking the final letter of speed

explanation.surface: A rock group high on ecstasy and amphetamines goes completely wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed' looks like the drug, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained and uninhibited behaviour, as in dancing with wild abandon.

clue.text: Flower festival not opening

indicators.note: not opening means without its first letter

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: A flower show that fails to open on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening' drops the first letter of EASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden plant, such as the Michaelmas daisy.

clue.text: Where to buy alcohol and chocolate snack

definitions.meaning: a pub counter or drinking establishment
a slab of chocolate, as in a Mars one

explanation.surface: Somewhere to get drinks and a sweet treat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a drinking place and an oblong of chocolate.

clue.text: Attractive person, one at centre of recent split-up

indicators.note: at centre of means placed in the middle of the scrambled word
split-up means broken apart, so the letters of recent are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A charmer finds themselves at the heart of a recent break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split-up' rearranges RECENT into ENTCER; 'at centre of' puts I in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lures or tempts others, a seducer.

clue.text: Shy crony, oddly

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd-numbered places

explanation.surface: A timid friend behaves strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of 'crony'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bashful or reserved in manner, a near synonym.

clue.text: Domineering woman misses a sign

indicators.note: misses means goes without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a virago is a bossy, domineering woman

explanation.surface: A bossy woman fails to notice a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses' drops A from VIRAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo, the virgin, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Dull-sounding poet

indicators.note: sounding means spoken aloud, so the dull colour is heard as a near-identical word

parts.note: dull, as of weather, means grey

explanation.surface: A poet whose verse sounds rather boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' signals that GREY is said aloud. Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray was an eighteenth-century English poet.

clue.text: Dad joining the French more than once to drink a beer

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: to drink means to take in, so the doubled article swallows the letter
more than once means the French article appears twice

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Dad keeps going for French lager, having a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than once' doubles LE; 'to drink' puts A inside, giving LEALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-coloured bitter-style brew, a type of beer.
